title: Spike: decode the current DAW's .asd (warp markers, mode, detune, loop) and test a hand-patched one
description:
## Intent
Answer M0 questions 1, 2 and 4 for the `.asd`: find where the current DAW version stores warp markers, warp on/off, warp mode, detune, start/end/loop, and the version marker; and check whether a hand-written `.asd` is honoured.

## Steps
1. Hex-diff the owner's reference files: same audio with different markers, modes and detune isolates each field.
2. Compare with the publicly documented older layouts (versions read by existing open-source parsers); note what moved.
3. Throwaway decoder in the scratchpad prints the markers of every reference `.asd`; they must equal the README table.
4. Hand-patch one `.asd` (move one marker), put it beside a fresh copy of the WAV, drag the WAV into the DAW: is the patched marker used? Repeat after changing the WAV's modification time, and with a copied WAV of a different length.
5. Record what triggers the DAW to rewrite the file.

## Output
A findings comment here and the `.asd` section of `design/daw-sidecars.md` §Formats (field, offset/encoding, versions, confidence).

## Verify (manual)
The scratch decoder's printout matches the fixture README for every reference `.asd`; the drag-in test result is recorded with the DAW version.

---
**Toolchain:** every Bash call starts with `export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`; run builds and tests under the watchdog: `safe-run.sh -- <command>` (6 GB / 20 min cap; do not edit it). At most two Rust-building agents at once.
**Protocol:** specs first (write the scenario, watch it fail, then code); keep a running log with `kbs comment` (decisions, problems, attempts, outcomes); paste the tail of **Verify** before asking for review; never commit, push or close (the reviewer does, after re-running Verify). Never write the DAW's brand name anywhere.

comments.text: Start (Spike Warp Sidecars): the DAW is not installed here and no owner reference files exist yet, so per the epic's 'Not blocked on the DAW' comment this pass decodes .asd files found in public repositories plus published community reverse-engineering, marks each finding provisional with the version it rests on, and leaves the hand-patch drag-in test for the licensed install.
